name: che-container-mcp
description: Run Linux container jobs, including long ones, through Apple's container CLI
long_description: An MCP server that wraps Apple's `container` CLI (tested with 1.7.1). container_run starts a one-off job from a local OCI image with a read-only source directory and a writable output directory and returns a job id at once; container_job_status, container_job_wait (bounded), container_job_result and container_job_cancel follow it. Job state is kept on disk, so jobs survive a restart of the server. The exit code is recorded by a /bin/sh wrapper, so images must contain /bin/sh. While a job runs, the server holds an idle-sleep assertion and reports whether the host slept. Docker is used only when a single container_run call passes allow_docker: true and `container` is unavailable. Requires macOS 26 with Apple Silicon and the container CLI installed.

tools.name: container_status
tools.description: Report the container service status, versions and kernel; optionally start the service

tools.name: container_image_ensure
tools.description: Make sure an image is local, pulling it when absent (returns pulling if the pull outlasts 600 seconds)

tools.name: container_run
tools.description: Start a one-off container job (source read-only at /src, output writable at /out) and return its job id at once

tools.name: container_job_status
tools.description: State of one job or of every job; running jobs include the last 20 log lines

tools.name: container_job_wait
tools.description: Wait for a job at most timeout_seconds; on timeout returns timed_out: true, not an error

tools.name: container_job_result
tools.description: Exit code, elapsed time, log tail and path, host sleep; deletes the job's container after copying its log

tools.name: container_job_cancel
tools.description: Stop a running job, copy its log and delete its container
